reason: A makes reasoning roles explicit without hiding them. Baseline answers offers the strongest continuous reading composition, although its legacy labels must not be treated as verified original questions. B check-in balances context and reachable outcomes most effectively across both text sizes. None demonstrates the authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold.
limitations: Assessment uses only the six attached sheets and supplied evidence descriptions. No implementation, other files, prior ratings or other graders were consulted.
Each score combines normal and 200% views. Component tuples use the same six dimensions as screen scores. A and F exclude null values; overall is 0.4A+0.6F.

Null feedback means no applicable feedback state was demonstrated for the shown reading or navigation component. It does not establish that interactive behavior is correct. Check-in feedback scores assess visible recovery guidance only.
Baseline browser checks are supplied evidence, not independently rerun here. Alternatives demonstrate layout proposals rather than actual outcome saving, inference, persistence or recovery.

Expanded disclosures, later passages, selected outcomes, keyboard focus, screen-reader semantics, loading, empty and error states are not shown. Exact target sizes and contrast were not independently measured.
The fixed tab bar reduces the visible reading area at 200%. These captures do not establish that content underneath it becomes unreachable; scrolling and bottom padding remain unverified.
Reason A depends on producer-supplied semantic roles; the necessary migration is not implemented. Its composition win is not implementation readiness.

No definitive hard-gate failure is established from these captures. No-horizontal-overflow and doubled text alone do not establish browser accessibility. Physical iPhone, VoiceOver and native behavior remain separately unverified.
